newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba denies it favours EMU delay, stands by treaty.
newsitem.headline: Buba denies it favours EMU delay, stands by treaty.

text.p: Germany's Bundesbank said on Sunday its president Hans Tietmeyer had not suggested a delay in the planned 1999 start date for European Monetary Union (EMU) and the bank stood by the Maastricht Treaty.

A spokesman for the bank, reading out a prepared statement from Tietmeyer by telephone to Reuters, also said the Bundesbank hoped the German government would respect its objections to a plan to revalue gold and currency reserves.
The Der Speigel news weekly, in an advance release from Monday's edition, had quoted Tietmeyer as asking whether Bonn and Paris could not postpone the start of EMU.
"Reports of suggestions by the Bundesbank or its president for a postponment of the start of the currency union are not accurate," the bank said in its statement.

The spokesman also said the bank's main objection to the revaluation plan were concerned primarily with effects on 1997 balance sheets and it hoped Bonn would give sufficient respect to these objections.
"The German Bundesbank naturally stands by the Maastricht Treaty," the spokesman quoted Tietmeyer as saying.
